payload.title: Compose an editable Markus homepage with reusable embedded listings
payload.description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a publication editor, I want homepage content and embedded listings to be authored as Markus composition, so that I can edit the homepage normally while shared constructs keep recent content current.

Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet):
```gherkin
Feature: Compose an editable Markus homepage with reusable embedded listings
  Scenario: Author homepage content and listings
    Given the homepage is the ordinary page at /
    When an authorized editor changes its Markus composition using supported reusable listing constructs
    Then authored content and embedded listings render together in the existing brand design
    And the theme supplies outer chrome without a bespoke Python homepage content-assembly function
    And the listing's selection parameters remain the sole truth for rendering and derived dependencies
  Scenario: Refresh composed pages after content changes
    Given one or several supported listing components occur in an authored page
    When the page is saved or compiled
    Then dependency extraction contributes their union to the generated reverse index
    When a published item is added, removed or changes type or featured state
    Then pages matching its old or new published state are refreshed through the shared post-save behavior
    And private drafts remain ineligible independently of listing selection
  Scenario: Change or remove the composition
    Given a page has generated listing dependency registrations
    When its composition changes or the page is deleted
    Then stale registrations are replaced or removed
    And editors do not maintain a parallel per-page predicate configuration
```

Approved unified page/wiki architecture, planning only: use one page/content system with paths. The homepage is an ordinary editable Markus page at `/`; product pages under `/features` and documentation under `/wiki` are ordinary content subtrees in that same system. Wiki denotes navigation and presentation, not a separate storage model, authoring backend, publication lifecycle or publishing engine. Reuse the existing content lifecycle, publishing projection and reader-access rules; avoid parallel site-versus-wiki systems and new content types unless a concrete need is demonstrated. A page's authored Markus composition owns its editable content and supported embedded listings; reusable themes retain outer chrome, branding and presentation. Existing routes, content, canonical/SEO metadata, heading/link behavior and brand design must be preserved through migration. Exact path schema, composition/listing syntax and Markus-versus-Papyrus extension ownership remain unresolved design work; do not invent current directives or claim they already exist.

Verified starting point: AnthusAI/Anth.us-web main 5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7 web/anthus_pages.py:404 homepage() assembles Python HTML, including three recent-post image cards plus seven dated links; web/build_via_papyrus.py:470 calls it and write_generated:704 wraps fragments directly through markus_shell.render_page. web/projector.py:369 uses generated-fragment digests for incremental inputs. This story plans migration of that custom content assembly to authored Markus plus reusable constructs; it does not assert existing generic syntax or reverse-index support. Preserve current render and SEO parity; unsupported custom dynamic query handling is an explicit design gap, not a promise to analyze arbitrary Python.
